At Rs.6,81,000/- Per Acre With All Statutory Benefits
And With Proportionate Cost.
This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing

, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the landlooser (since deceased represented by legal representatives) seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Bidar (henceforth referred to as 'reference Court') in LAC No.129/2006 vide its judgment and order dated 21.12.2013.

2. The landlooser is the owner of the land bearing Sy.No.3 of Mirjapur-T village measuring 4 acres 10 guntas which was proposed for acquisition in terms of notification NC: 2023:KHC-K:5350 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (henceforth referred to as 'Act') dated 22.06.2004 published on 15.07.2004 for the purpose of construction of irrigation tank at Astur village.
The market value of the land was determined by the Land Acquisition Officer in terms of an award dated 30.06.2005 and the compensation was determined at Rs.48,719/- per acre.
3. Feeling aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the landlooser sought reference under Section 18(1) of the Act.
The reference Court after considering the oral and documentary evidence adduced before it, enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.4,35,600/- per acre.

The reference Court considered the compensation determined in LAC No.8/2006, which was in respect of acquisition of land in Mirjapur-T village in terms of a notification dated 22.06.2004 published on 15.07.2004 and held that the landloosers are entitled to a sum of Rs.4,35,600/- per acre along with all statutory benefits.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, the landlooser has filed this appeal.
5. During the pendency of this appeal, the appellant/landlooser died and her legal representatives are brought on record.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellants/landloosers contends that the judgment of the reference Court in LAC No.8/2006 was challenged before this Court in MFA No.30878/2013 and that this Court in terms of the judgment dated 04.07.2016 enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.6,81,000/- per acre which was based upon the judgment of this Court in MFA Nos.30573/2013 and 30877/2013.
He further contends that the appeal filed by the State challenging the judgment awarded by the reference Court in the instant case in MFA No.30607/2011 was dismissed.
He therefore prays that the compensation be enhanced to a sum of Rs.6,81,000/- per acre.

The learned High Court Government Pleader, on the other hand, did not dispute that in respect of the very same acquisition and for the same village, the compensation in respect of Mirjapur-T village is enhanced to a sum of Rs.6,81,000/- by this Court in MFA No.30878/2013.
8.
In that view of the matter, this appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.4,35,600/- per acre awarded by the reference Court is modified and enhanced to a sum of Rs.6,81,000/- per acre along with all statutory benefits, cost and interest.
However, the appellants/landloosers are not entitled to interest for the delayed period of 931 days as ordered by this Court on 17.11.2017.
